package_info.package_manager: Windows executable (malware builder: Chaos Builder v3, Mercurial Grabber icon)
package_info.package_versions: All known variants (not versioned in the traditional sense, but includes both older and newer variants as described)
package_info.why_malicious: The DoDo ransomware encrypts and exfiltrates victims’ files, demands ransom for decryption and to prevent data leaks, and irreversibly overwrites files larger than 1MB, functioning as a wiper. It masquerades as legitimate or malicious tools (e.g., Mercurial Grabber), deceiving users into execution.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (user execution of the downloaded file)
execution_context.file_location: Windows PE executable (masquerading as Mercurial Grabber or other tools)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Encrypt files smaller than 1MB; overwrite files larger than 1MB; add .dodov2 or .crypterdodo extension; drop ransom note (dodov2_readit.txt or PLEASEREAD.txt); replace desktop wallpaper; exfiltrate stolen files.
malicious_snippets.code_language: C# (compiled to Windows PE executable via Chaos Builder v3)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code enumerates user files, encrypts files smaller than 1MB, overwrites files larger than 1MB, appends a custom extension, drops a ransom note, changes the desktop wallpaper, and exfiltrates stolen files to the attacker, resulting in data loss and extortion.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Encrypting and overwriting user files, dropping ransom notes, and exfiltrating data are classic ransomware behaviors. The overwriting of large files acts as a wiper, causing irreversible data loss.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal applications do not encrypt or overwrite user files, nor do they demand ransom or exfiltrate data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Encryption utilities may encrypt files, but only with user consent and without ransom demands or data exfiltration.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (user execution of the downloaded file)
execution_context.file_location: Windows PE executable (masquerading as Mercurial Grabber or other tools)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Steal Discord tokens, machine information, Windows product keys, and Chrome passwords using built-in Mercurial Grabber functions.
malicious_snippets.code_language: C# (compiled to Windows PE executable via Mercurial Grabber builder)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code accesses sensitive information such as Discord tokens, system information, product keys, and browser passwords, then exfiltrates this data to the attacker’s server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Harvesting and exfiltrating credentials and sensitive information is a hallmark of infostealer malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not access or transmit user credentials or system secrets without explicit user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise management tools may inventory system information, but not exfiltrate credentials or tokens.
key_indicators: Access to Discord tokens and browser passwords

attack_chain.action: User downloads and executes a file masquerading as Mercurial Grabber or another tool.
Malware harvests sensitive information (Discord tokens, product keys, Chrome passwords) and exfiltrates it to the attacker.
Malware enumerates user files, encrypts files smaller than 1MB, overwrites larger files, appends custom extension, drops ransom note, and changes desktop wallpaper.
attack_chain.leads_to: Data loss, extortion, and user notification

behavioral_signatures: Mass file encryption with custom extension (.dodov2, .crypterdodo)
Changing desktop wallpaper to ransom message
Harvesting and exfiltrating credentials (Discord tokens, browser passwords)
file_indicators: Desktop wallpaper replaced with ransom message
network_indicators: Outbound connections to attacker-controlled servers for exfiltration
Potential use of Discord webhooks or other C2 infrastructure
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for mass file modifications with new extensions (.dodov2, .crypterdodo), creation of ransom notes, and changes to desktop wallpaper. Detect processes accessing and exfiltrating browser passwords, Discord tokens, or product keys. Watch for suspicious outbound network connections following file encryption or credential harvesting. Use AV/EDR signatures for known ransomware families (Chaos Builder, Mercurial Grabber).
